# Generated by care-pi from /etc/care-pi/config.yaml. Do not edit.
# The pod "care" shares one network namespace. The containers talk over localhost.
# Do not start or stop care-pod.service directly. Use care.target.

[Unit]
Description=care-pi pod (shared localhost of the CARE containers)
PartOf=care.target
# The pod publishes on the LAN addresses, so it starts after the network is up.
# Quadlet adds these two lines by default too. care-start.service does not wait for the network.
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target
# Tailscale mode: the pod also publishes on the address of tailscale0 (docs/connectivity.md).
After=tailscaled.service

[Pod]
PodName=care
# HTTP, HTTPS, and the console (S48) on each LAN IPv4 address, never on 0.0.0.0.
PublishPort=192.168.1.10:80:80
PublishPort=192.168.1.10:443:443
PublishPort=192.168.1.10:8443:8443
PublishPort=10.0.0.5:80:80
PublishPort=10.0.0.5:443:443
PublishPort=10.0.0.5:8443:8443
# The same ports on the Tailscale address (P11). The LAN list above stays the list for default_sni and avahi.
PublishPort=100.101.102.103:80:80
PublishPort=100.101.102.103:443:443
PublishPort=100.101.102.103:8443:8443
# Debug ports on the host loopback only: API and object storage.
PublishPort=127.0.0.1:19000:9000
PublishPort=127.0.0.1:17070:7070

[Service]
# At the boot, tailscaled sets the address of tailscale0 some seconds after its start. Wait for it, at most
# 30s; then start in any case. net.ipv4.ip_nonlocal_bind (/etc/sysctl.d/50-care-pi.conf) lets the pod
# publish on an address that is not there (an expired node key, no control server): the publish works when it comes.
ExecStartPre=-/usr/local/bin/care-pi network wait-address --address 100.101.102.103 --timeout 30s
